summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease was admitted with chest and bilateral knee pain consistent with a vaso-occlusive crisis, triggered by community-acquired pneumonia. She presented with fever, leukocytosis, and a new left lower lobe infiltrate on chest X-ray. She was treated with a seven-day course of levofloxacin, IV fluids, oxygen supplementation, and IV hydromorphone, transitioning to oral pain control by discharge. Her condition improved with resolution of fever, stable hemoglobin without transfusion, and successful weaning from oxygen. She was discharged home in stable condition on her baseline hydroxyurea and folic acid regimen, with instructions to continue oral and intramuscular hydromorphone as needed for pain.
